text: Your iPhone and your friend's Android are right next to each other.
Sending one file between them takes over three minutes.
The only thing both phones can talk over is Bluetooth, and Bluetooth crawls at about five kilobytes a second.
So we built Fast Link into the Offline Protocol SDK.
Step one: the phones find each other over Bluetooth and set up an end-to-end encrypted session.
Step two: the app asks for a fast link, and the Android phone spins up its own private Wi-Fi network, with a brand new random password made just for this link.
Step three: that password goes to the iPhone inside the encrypted session. Nobody else ever sees it.
Step four: the iPhone joins, the phones open a direct Wi-Fi stream, and each one proves who it is before a single byte moves.
Bluetooth stays on the whole time, so no message drops during the switch.
We tested it on a Samsung and an iPhone 16.
A one megabyte file over Bluetooth took one hundred ninety-seven seconds.
Over Fast Link it took two and a half.
Getting the link up takes about ten seconds and one tap on the iPhone. When you leave the app or stop sending, it shuts itself down.
No router. No internet. No cloud. Just two phones. Offline Protocol.
tag: NO ROUTER · NO INTERNET · NO CLOUD
